description: dryvist/.github master Renovate grouping preset — single source of truth for dependency grouping across all dryvist and JacobPEvans repos.

Batches related dependency updates into single PRs to reduce review burden and prevent deploy-queue saturation. Extended by renovate-presets.json — do not extend this directly from consumers, extend renovate-presets instead. Adding a new ecosystem grouping? Add a packageRule here with a clear description explaining why the packages must move together.

packageRules.description: Fallback grouping for .nix custom-regex version pins: batch each repo's **/*.nix custom.regex pins into one scheduled, auto-merged 'nix version pins' PR (minor/patch) so slow-moving pins don't each take a branch/PR slot and starve (e.g. nix-ai huggingface-hub stalled at 1.15.0 for ~6 weeks, breaking the hf CLI). Placed FIRST so the more specific ecosystem groups below (HuggingFace, OpenTelemetry, ...) still override groupName for their packages, and repo-specific interlock groups (e.g. nix-ai mlx-core, evaluated last in the consuming repo) still win. Scoped to **/*.nix so the Ansible-YAML and Docker-image custom.regex managers are unaffected. Majors excluded so they open individually under the 30-day major-default hold. Auto-merge here mirrors the publisher-agnostic minor/patch rule in renovate-presets.json (any package, any ecosystem, 3-day stabilization + green CI) — it is not a trust carve-out, just keeping grouped members on the same auto-merge behavior as every other minor/patch update. PR-creation cadence for custom.regex members (Fri ~15:00/Mon ~05:00 ET) also comes from renovate-presets.json.
Group OpenTofu/Terraform providers and modules into a single PR. Prevents deploy-queue saturation when related provider and module bumps arrive together.

Group Ansible Galaxy collection updates. Collections almost always release together (e.g., community.general + ansible.posix) and breakage manifests at the playbook level, so reviewing them as a unit is correct.
Group OpenTelemetry packages across npm and Python. OTel releases SDKs in lockstep — mixing versions across instrumentation packages causes silent dropped spans.

Group TypeScript type definitions (@types/*). Type-only updates are mechanical and almost never break runtime behavior. Auto-merge here is just the publisher-agnostic minor/patch rule in renovate-presets.json (any package, any ecosystem, 3-day stabilization + green CI) applied to the grouped batch — not a trust carve-out for @types/*.

Group ESLint core and TypeScript-aware ESLint plugins. typescript-eslint releases as a monorepo with matched versions across @typescript-eslint/parser, @typescript-eslint/eslint-plugin, etc. — they must move together.
Group pytest core and pytest-* plugins. Plugin compatibility is tied to pytest minor versions; batching prevents version-skew breakages in CI.
Group AWS SDK packages across npm (@aws-sdk/*, aws-sdk) and Python (boto3, botocore). AWS releases these as a coordinated set — botocore feeds boto3, @aws-sdk submodules share a version.
Group HuggingFace ecosystem packages. transformers + tokenizers + datasets + accelerate + huggingface-hub have tightly-coupled version requirements; partial updates routinely break imports.

First-party reusable workflows: one PR per repository for dryvist/.github and dryvist/ai-workflows github-actions updates. Majors are excluded and open individually. Auto-merge and labels come from the dryvist/** rules in renovate-presets.json; Renovate auto-merges a grouped branch only when every update in it auto-merges and unions their labels, so a group holding a minor bump stays open with bump:minor.
